name: Durability
summary: Once data is acknowledged as written, it survives failures without loss — backed by replicated storage, commit logs, snapshots, and backups.
description: Durability is the guarantee that committed data will not be lost when hardware, processes, or whole regions fail. In data architectures it rests on the storage foundation: object stores offering eleven nines of durability, write-ahead and commit logs that make writes recoverable, replication factors that keep multiple copies, and table-format snapshots that let you recover to any prior state. Architectures rooted in durable object storage and audit-preserving models are strongest; ephemeral in-memory or single-node state is durable only insofar as it is backed by a persistent log.

mechanisms.name: Object-storage eleven-nines
mechanisms.note: Landing data on cloud object storage that replicates every object across devices and facilities for 99.999999999% durability.

mechanisms.name: Write-ahead / commit logs
mechanisms.note: Persisting every change to an ordered log before acknowledging it, so committed writes survive a crash and can be replayed.

mechanisms.name: Replication factor
mechanisms.note: Keeping N copies of each partition or block across nodes so the loss of a disk or machine never loses acknowledged data.

mechanisms.name: Snapshots and time-travel
mechanisms.note: Table-format snapshots retain prior versions, letting you recover an accidentally deleted or corrupted table to an earlier state.

mechanisms.name: Backups and cross-region replication
mechanisms.note: Copying data to an independent region or backup so a regional failure or catastrophic error doesn't destroy the only copy.

manifestations.statement: Every layer persists to eleven-nines object storage, and table-format snapshots keep prior versions, so acknowledged data survives node and region failures and a bad write can be rolled back to a durable snapshot.

Data lives once on durable object storage with immutable snapshots and manifest history; deletes and updates create new snapshots, so nothing acknowledged is silently lost and any prior state is recoverable.
The lake's whole premise is cheap, durable landing on object storage that replicates every object across facilities — raw data, once written, is about as safe from loss as any storage on offer.

Insert-only hubs, links, and satellites never overwrite history, so the model preserves a durable, auditable record of every version — durability is reinforced by the modelling discipline, not just the storage.

Managed warehouses replicate storage and take automatic snapshots with time-travel, so committed dimensional data survives failures and can be restored to a prior point without a separate backup process.
The cloud warehouse durably replicates all committed tables and offers time-travel recovery, so loaded raw data and dbt-built marts survive hardware failures and accidental drops alike.
Continuous commits land in a durable table format on object storage with retained snapshots, so even minutes-fresh data is persisted safely and recoverable to any recent version.
The replicated, retained commit log durably stores every event until its retention or compaction policy expires, so consumers can always recover acknowledged events from the log.

The warehouse target is durable, but durability of the change stream is bounded by source log retention — if the CDC pipeline lags past the retention window, unshipped changes can be lost before landing.
Once telemetry reaches the replicated ingest log and object storage it is durable, but data buffered on devices or in edge gateways before ingest can be lost if a device fails before flushing.

The source log is durable and replicated, but the streaming operators' working state is ephemeral in memory — durability holds only because that state can be rebuilt by replaying the durable log, not because it is itself persisted.
Serving engines often hold hot data in memory or on local disk for speed, so durability of the serving copy is limited; it is backstopped by the durable upstream log or lake it can reload from.

The offline feature store on the lake is durable, but the online store is frequently an in-memory or cache tier optimized for low-latency reads, so its copy is durable only as a re-materialization of the offline source.
By design the federation layer holds no copy at all, so it contributes zero durability — the guarantee is entirely delegated to whatever source systems the query touches.
Data sits in local files on a single node with no replication; durability is only as good as that one disk and whatever manual backup the operator arranges, so hardware loss can mean data loss.

The activation loop is a transient push of warehouse data into SaaS tools; it holds no durable copy of what it sends, and any record of what was pushed depends on logging, not on a persisted store of the payloads.
The metrics layer stores definitions, not data, and computes results on demand, so it has little durable state of its own beyond the versioned metric definitions in source control.
Sensitive data rests on durable governed storage, but tokenization introduces a vault whose loss or drift can render protected values unrecoverable if not itself backed up.

tradeoffs.title: Latency
tradeoffs.note: Guaranteeing data survives means synchronously replicating and fsync-ing writes to stable storage before acknowledging, which adds measurable latency to every durable write.

tradeoffs.title: Cost efficiency
tradeoffs.note: Durability keeps multiple copies, cross-region replication, and layered backups, so protecting every byte against loss multiplies storage and transfer spend.

tradeoffs.title: Throughput
tradeoffs.note: Requiring acknowledged, fully persisted writes before proceeding throttles ingest, so the safest durable path accepts fewer records per second than unacknowledged writes.
